name: Two-way light switch plan mark
summary: Plan mark for a two-way switch used in pairs so one lighting group can be switched from two places.
description: Two-way switches are installed in pairs at either end of a corridor or staircase so either switch changes the state of the lights. The IEC-style plan form draws the switch circle with strokes in two opposite directions, each with a tick, showing the changeover action.

On a plan the pair is linked by a switching line to the luminaire group. The electrician reads the pair to run strappers between the two switches; where an intermediate switch is shown between them, a third location can also control the lights.
The symbol does not show the wiring method, which can be conventional strappers or a converted arrangement. It also does not tell you the gang count unless written.
readingNotes: Expect two-way switches in pairs; a single two-way switch usually signals a drafting error or a spare.
Look for an intermediate switch between the pair on long runs.
drawingChecklist: Show both switch positions and the controlled luminaires.
Note gang count where plates are shared.
distinction: In US terminology this is a three-way switch; the US four-way switch corresponds to the IEC intermediate switch.
